newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after firmer ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after firmer ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Tuesday following a stronger ACCESS session, trade sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.465 to $2.47 after settling to the downside Monday at $2.426 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September last traded 1.4 cents firmer at $2.44.

This morning cash prices at Henry Hub were talked about five cents higher in the low-$2.60s, while early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association's storage report were about 62 bcf, traders said.
Technically, September resistance was pegged at $2.53, $2.55 and the contract high at $2.605. Support was seen at Friday's low of $2.395 and then at $2.34 and $2.30.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed three cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were steady to up slightly in the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas also was modestly higher in the mid-to-high $2.70s.

Cooler-than-normal weather is forecast to continue throughout the Northeast and Midwest this week, while in the southern plains and Texas most temperatures are expected to hover a couple of degrees above normal, according to Weather Services Corp.
